<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s).

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2212b16988df69afb7272a2829099ac9ad0ca98d`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2212b16988df69afb7272a2829099ac9ad0ca98d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ecc43a1a8e339d02bee9c04978ca64016beaf03b` — the merge of head `4bfe46dc534ebaea879becc8879f40c5f3316da0` into base `2212b16988df69afb7272a2829099ac9ad0ca98d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ecc43a1a8e339d02bee9c04978ca64016beaf03b && git checkout ecc43a1a8e339d02bee9c04978ca64016beaf03b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2212b16988df69afb7272a2829099ac9ad0ca98d 4bfe46dc534ebaea879becc8879f40c5f3316da0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2212b16988df69afb7272a2829099ac9ad0ca98d && git merge --no-ff 4bfe46dc534ebaea879becc8879f40c5f3316da0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2212b16988df69afb7272a2829099ac9ad0ca98d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2212b16988df69afb7272a2829099ac9ad0ca98d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Inputs: card #33787 (body and all 30 comments), PR #36116 (body, 32-file list, net diff of merge base `78437e20d7` against the head) and the head's check-runs. The narrowing arm is declared, so the whole diff outside the changeset is in scope. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `packages/objectql/src/fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts`, `fixed-read-leaf-position.ts`, `engine-secrets-and-routing.ts`, `engine-datasource-routing.ts`, `packages/core/src/hook-dispatch.ts`, `kernel.ts`, `security/lifecycle-verb-rls-operation.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/shared-record-ids.ts`, `fixed-read-leaf.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts`, `read-audit.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts`, `rule-hooks.ts`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The two scopes change shape for every sharing-scoped caller.** `buildReadFilter` answers `$or` of the owner match, the queue match, `{ id: { $in: SharedRecordIds.read(object, user) } }` and the approval ids; `buildWriteFilter` answers the update form with `.write(object, user, WRITE_ACCESS_LEVELS)`, and `delete` the owner match alone. This is ADR-0155 D3 as written, the approval ids a disjunct of their own. A caller with no grant now gets the `$or` where it got the bare owner match. Right, and a narrowing for any consumer that matched the old shape (the dogfood pin was one).
- **Grants past 5,000 count.** The capped read and `grantedRecordIds` are gone from both builders; no other gate read the list. Right: the card's defect.
- **R2: share grants stop counting where storage cannot evaluate the leaf.** `shareGrantsInertReason` answers for an object on another datasource (the engine's own `fixedReadLeafClassOf`) and for a driver without the declaration (the seam's own `driverEvaluatesFixedReadLeaf`); both are the readings `passFixedReadLeaves` makes at read, so the producer and the seam cannot disagree on a top-level read. There: no share arm on either scope, `checkEdit` reads no grant, `grant` refuses for system and direct callers, the rule save door refuses (`sharingRuleObjectRefusal`, 422), the object picker drops the object, and the boot names holders once at `warn`. Right, a narrowing, ruled (6942854600, with 7045701086 and seat call 7060526112 for driver-memory).
- **The D7 order is kept.** The storage arm is asked last in `inertGrantReason`, so bypass, `controlled_by_parent`, public, owner-less and phantom-anchor refusals keep their shipped reason; on a public object the external floor (#25549) lifts only where storage evaluates the leaf. Right.
- **R1 at boot.** A `kernel:bootstrapped` handler throws `fixedReadLeafRefusal` (`INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500) when the engine recognises a registration for `sys_record_share` by name. The boot-phase dispatch propagates the first throw on both kernels (`dispatchHookPropagating`), so the boot does fail. plugin-audit installs its `afterFind` hook in `kernel:ready`, before this handler, so the opt-in named in the contract is caught at boot. Right, a narrowing, ruled.
- **A registration naming no object no longer runs on the share arm.** Nothing refuses or logs it; the contract and the changeset tell it. Right as ruled (D4's boundary).
- **`ctx.ast.filter` is no longer written** by the read and bulk-write merges. Plan step 6 allows it. Right.
- **`SharingService` gains two public members** (`shareGrantsInertReason`, `inertShareGrantHolders`) and `SharingEngine` two optional ones. Additive. plugin-security reaches `shareGrantsInertReason` by feature test, as it already reaches `listApprovalReadGrants`; neither is on `ISharingService`. Right.
- **`security/explain` output.** On an R2 object each share is `neutral` and the sharing layer's detail gains one sentence with the reason; the record's `rowFilter` there is the owner match. Right.
- **`packages/spec`: comments only.** The 31+ / 24- in `contracts/sharing-service.ts` is jsdoc; no type, schema or export moves. Right.
- **Inherited envelopes.** On an Oracle `RAW(16)` key a grant whose `record_id` the list refused with 400 now fails the statement with 500 (#36001, seat-accepted in 7058138586 and 7058625670). Right as inherited.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch` and `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`. Right: AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 ships a non-protocol change, breaking included, as `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition, and both are present (`fix(plugin-sharing)!`, three BREAKING bullets each with its host remedy, marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).

`Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no authorable key, accepted value or default moves (ADR-0155 "Leaves unchanged"), and the change is a service's enforcement.

Clause-②: `yes (narrowing)`, line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, the same value in both. Right: R2, the two doors' refusals and the boot refusal each take away something that worked.

`@objectstack/spec` (jsdoc) and the published skills text move without being named; both sit in the fixed group and version with the two named packages. `Check Changeset` is green twice on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dogfood pin outside the claim's surface**: answered. Maintainer 「同意」 (amendment 7061720534); the diff is the one line named there.
- **driver-memory under R2**: answered by ruling 7045701086 and seat call 7060526112. The ADR text was not brought along: see S1.
- **PostgreSQL 16 plans the total of a caller with no grant as a sequential scan** (1.46 to 7.29 ms at 100k, 7.88 to 42.21 ms at 1M): answered by seat call 7060526112, stated in the changeset, follow-up #36034. ADR-0155 D6 asks the switch to quote that reading, and it does.
- **The three #35906 preconditions**: carried into the changeset. The Oracle `RAW(16)` envelope change (7058138586, 7058625670, 7060497587) is in the PR body only; the changeset is the seat's ACCEPT to read.
- **O8 census, cloud half: escalated.** ADR-0155's acceptance criteria and plan step 6 say the switch card is not cut without the census, and amendment 7061720534 says the push stays held until the cloud half is in. The card body records objectstack and hotcrm, and says the cloud half moved to #36115 on the maintainer's word of 2026-11-21 14:43 UTC. No card comment records that word or releases the hold; the body's quotation is the only record in this review's inputs. The hand that lands this Tier H PR confirms it. cloud pins objectstack by version, so nothing reaches it before its own bump.
- **Dogfood battery (owed by the narrowing arm)**: the PR body's run is of the local build on base `c00be39b74`, not of this head. On a `pull_request` event the three dogfood shards are skipped by design and `Dogfood Regression Gate` is a rollup, so this head's battery is the merge queue's.
- **Showcase `Schema sync FAILED` seen in the dogfood log, not filed**: outside this diff; the seat's filing gate decides.
- **PR author**: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- **SQL push-down**: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The diff removes the one this card is about: no grant is read into memory and nothing binds a parameter per grant. The approval ids stay a list (ADR-0155 D3, O4). `inertShareGrantHolders` makes one `limit 1` read per R2 object at boot and none on a host whose objects all sit beside `sys_record_share` on a SQL driver. `checkEdit` keeps its one-record probe.
- **Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-21T15:02Z.** Success: Lint & Repo Gates and all eight `Lint ·` jobs, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected by code changes, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Test Core (4/10), (6/10), (7/10), (8/10), and the Dogfood Regression Gate rollup. **Still in progress, so no verdict yet:** Build Core; Test Core 1, 2, 3, 5, 9 and 10 of 10; Type Check · workspace; Type Check · consumer gates; Type Check UI; Build & E2E UI; Test UI 1 to 16 of 16. Skipped on this event: the dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Build Docs, Lint UI, UI Published Artifacts. No check-run has failed. The verdict below is of the tree; the suites that pin it have not all reported.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts`** holds, sentence by sentence, against `plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts` and `share-arm-boot.ts`.

- "carries the read scope's share arm as a `SharedRecordIds` leaf" and "the predicate-update scope carries the write form": `buildReadFilter`, `buildWriteFilter`.
- "writes no share arm and reads no grant row": both builders and `checkEdit` ask `shareGrantsInertReason` first.
- "its grant and sharing-rule doors refuse": `assertNotInertGrant` runs for system callers too; `sharingRuleObjectRefusal` at `defineRule` and at the `sys_sharing_rule` hook.
- "R1 at boot, so the host does not start": holds, see ①.
- The no-object paragraph: no engine read of `sys_record_share` remains in either builder.
- `buildReadFilter`'s and `grant`'s jsdoc say the same as the code.

**`docs/adr/0155-...md`.** The dated note is true: `grantedRecordIds` is gone from the tree outside this record, D2 names it bare, and the blank-id guard is declared with `fixed-read-leaf.ts#FixedInnerRead`. The line-160 edit removes only the dead anchor and the note says so. Against its first consumer the record does not hold in one place:

S1 (should-fix) — ADR-0155 still records `driver-memory` as evaluating the leaf, and this head ships it under R2 with no note. D5's row reads "evaluates in process" and "the row stands as stated here"; Q2 closes with "`driver-memory` is not in this census; its row stands as D5 states it"; plan step 6 says "⛔ It lands last". At this head `driver-memory` declares no `fixedReadLeaves`, so `shareGrantsInertReason` makes its share grants inert, and the changeset names the in-memory driver beside MongoDB and OData. The authority exists (maintainer 7045701086, step 4 on hold; seat call 7060526112) but lives on the card only. Prime Directive 13 asks a moved decision to be recorded on the record. This PR already edits the file under Tier H: it owes a second dated, append-only note saying that step 4 (#35873) is on hold, that the switch landed before it on ruling 7045701086, and that `driver-memory` takes R2 until a driver declares the leaf.

**`skills/objectstack-data/rules/datasources.md`.** The sentence is true of the code: grants count only beside `sys_record_share` on a driver that declares the leaf, and today only the SQL family does (`driver-sql`, with sqlite-wasm and Turso inheriting). It sits in the paragraph that tells an author when to declare a separate datasource, which is where the consequence belongs. It teaches sharing behaviour, hence `Security-touching: yes`. The trims keep every identifier eval cases 3 and 11 grade on. The card carries no eval prompt, and the PR states the eval round was not run.

**Implementing files.**

- `sharing-service.ts`: agrees with D3, R2 and ADR-0111 D7. A recognition that throws counts as no answer and the leaf is written with the seam behind it; an engine with no driver for the object answers R2. `sharingRuleObjectRemedy` follows the verdict's order.
- `sharing-plugin.ts` and `share-arm-boot.ts`: the R1 handler is registered ahead of the plugin's other `kernel:bootstrapped` passes; the report runs in a handler of its own and cannot fail the boot. The bulk-write merge reaches only `update` and `delete`: `restore` and `purge` dispatch with no AST and return early, so the write form never lands on a verb the seam refuses.
- `explain-engine.ts`, `security-plugin-explain-access.ts`: the reason is asked of the sharing service, never restated; a throw is no answer.
- Testkits and updated tests: each double resolves the leaf under `fixedInnerReadOf`, not a restated predicate, and throws on a leaf outside `$in`. `shared-record-ids-switch.test.ts` carries every D6 pin: 5,000 parity on list total and GET per arm, 5,001, 6,000, both scopes, nested, delegated.
- The two anchor files and the conformance-test comment say what the code does.

Attempts to break it that did not: a stale AST-keyed cache (none in objectql, driver-sql, rest, runtime or plugin-security); an in-process matcher fed the scope in production code (only the explainer, which resolves the leaf at the record); a hook that names the share table registered after the boot check (the seam refuses at read, as the contract says); the delegator leg's recipient (the seam admits `onBehalfOf.userId`).

S2 (should-fix) — D6's PostgreSQL cell has no reading at this head. Ruling 6895275749 and ADR-0155 D6 ask for parity "on SQLite and on PostgreSQL". The cell is `describe.skipIf` on `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`, and no job provisions that variable for plugin-sharing (the test file's own header says so; `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is skipped on this event and does not run this package). The only PostgreSQL run is the dev's, taken before both rebases. Owed: the 18-test file run with the variable set at the head that lands, its reading recorded on the PR. That needs no tree change; S1's fix moves the head anyway. Wiring the cell into the live-PG job is a workflow edit and a follow-up card.

Nits, none affecting correctness or the contract:

- N1 — `sharing-plugin.ts`: the `sys_record_share` self-scope branch still mirrors its scope under `ast.filter`, while the two new comments say no driver reads that key. No leaf sits there, so plan step 6 is met. Follow-up or accepted.
- N2 — the skill sentence's "(422)" is what the grant door and the rule save door answer. A rule declared in a stack's `sharingRules` meets no door: its reconcile pass aborts with the same code in the log (`sharing-rule-service.ts#grantOrAbsorbOrganizationRefusal`). The takeaway holds. The same hunk deletes "Federation is read-only by default.", leaving the default to the heading "double opt-in"; eval case 3 expects the write gate left closed. Accepted, or a follow-up with an eval round.
- N3 — spec and engine prose outside this diff still speaks of the list in the present: `packages/spec/src/data/shared-record-ids.ts` ("where today's list of granted ids sits", "the list the share arm binds today holds at most 5,000") and `packages/objectql/src/fixed-read-leaf-seam.ts` ("until then nothing on main writes the leaf"). The same class as the four texts amendment 7060526112 called due. Follow-up card.
- N4 — the nested and delegated pins assert absolute counts above the cap, where D6 words them as "the rows today's lists answer below the cap". The expected values are fixed by the fixture. Accepted.

No must-fix. Two should-fix, S1 and S2, open on this head.

  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code

  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — a `hits` path sits on the low-risk skills arm: when the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/1cb35bdc-0d81-5349-bc14-73d1d05fc076/scratchpad/pr-36116/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
